react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on the same biological story: the one-carbon folate cycle and its intersection with amino-acid metabolism are the dominant perturbed subsystem. RaMP multi-DB ORA (merged KEGG+SMPDB) ranked Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260) first with an FDR of 8.6e-17 and 7/57 metabolites hit, driven by glycine, serine, threonine, cysteine, choline, adenosine and S-adenosyl-L-methionine. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently ranked the identical KEGG:hsa00260 pathway second (p = 3.3e-7), with glycine, serine, threonine, cysteine and choline as hits. The m/z-direct mummichog network also placed the matched KEGG:map00260 pathway (reported as 'Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism' in MUMM namespace) at rank 1 (p = 0.0046), with a perfect 8-of-8 overlap. Methionine metabolism (KEGG:map00270 / hsa00270) appears as the second cross-paradigm winner: rank 9 in RaMP (FDR = 1.1e-14) and rank 2 in MetaboAnalystR (p = 6e-4), with S-adenosyl-L-methionine, L-serine and L-cysteine as shared driver metabolites. Folate one-carbon metabolism (KEGG:hsa00670) emerged uniquely in MetaboAnalystR at rank 1 (p = 8.4e-10), placing glycine, SAM, choline, serine, adenosine and cysteine as a coherent six-metabolite hit that bridges the folate cycle to the methyl-donor economy. Choline appears as a hub metabolite linking glycine/serine metabolism, glycerophospholipid metabolism (mummichog rank 4) and the folate cycle, consistent with its role as an methyl-group donor upstream of methionine and SAM. The phenylacetaldehyde (KEGG:C04043) was captured in tyrosine metabolism (mummichog rank 6, p = 0.052), reflecting its origin from aromatic amino-acid catabolism. Together, these results indicate that the treatment strongly dysregulates one-carbon/folate metabolism and its downstream methylation capacity, with serine and SAM as the primary driver metabolites connecting glycine/serine/threonine metabolism to the universal methyl-donor cycle.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on amino-acid metabolism as the dominant perturbed subsystem. RaMP ORA against the merged pathway library ranked KEGG:map00260 'Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism' first (FDR 8.6e-17; 7-of-57 input metabolites hit) and KEGG:map00270 'Methionine Metabolism' ninth (FDR 1.05e-14; 6-of-51 input metabolites hit). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently ranked KEGG:hsa00670 first (p=8.357e-10; 6 hits: glycine, serine, choline, adenosine, cysteine, SAM) and KEGG:hsa00260 second (p=3.3e-7; 5 hits: serine, glycine, threonine, choline, cysteine). The m/z-direct mummichog network confirmed this pattern: MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism ranked first (p=0.0016; 8-of-8 overlap) and MUMM:methionine_and_cysteine_metabolism ranked second (p=0.0084; 6-of-6 overlap). The WikiPathways 'Cysteine and methionine catabolism' (WP:WP4504) also reached significance (FDR 3.0e-12; 5 hits). Glycine (KEGG:C00037), L-serine (KEGG:C00065), choline (KEGG:C00114), L-threonine (KEGG:C00188), and L-cysteine (KEGG:C00097) are driver metabolites shared across the amino-acid cluster. S-Adenosylmethionine (KEGG:C00019) additionally anchors the methyl-donor subsystem within methionine metabolism. Tyrosine metabolism (MUMM:tyrosine_metabolism) captured the 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde input (KEGG:C04043) with a 3-of-3 metabolite overlap (p=0.047). Glycerophospholipid metabolism (MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism) was a shared network hit through choline and serine. The treatment broadly dysregulates the interconnected amino-acid/methyl-donor metabolic network spanning glycine-serine-threonine metabolism and methionine-cysteine metabolism.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on amino-acid metabolism as the dominant perturbed subsystem in the treatment group. RaMP multi-database ORA ranked KEGG:map00260 "Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism" first with FDR 8.6e-17 and 7 of the input metabolites as hits (glycine, choline, adenosine, L-serine, L-cysteine, L-threonine, and S-adenosylmethionine). The same ORA ranked KEGG:map00270 "Methionine Metabolism" ninth with FDR 1.05e-14 and 6 hits, while the MUMM namespace network from mummichog confirmed glycine-serine-alanine-threonine metabolism as the top network hit (p=0.004, 8-of-8 metabolite overlap) and methionine-and-cysteine-metabolism second (p=0.013, 6-of-6 overlap). Tyrosine metabolism captured the 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde input in the mummichog network (p=0.053, 3-of-3 overlap). The convergence across ORA and m/z-directed network paradigms identifies glycine, L-serine, and S-adenosylmethionine as the primary driver metabolites, connected through enzymes SHMT (R01500), GNMT (R04285), CBS (R01127), and MAT1A (R00587) that convert serine, glycine, and methionine into methyl-donor intermediates. The treatment group therefore shows a coordinated perturbation of one-carbon amino-acid metabolism and methyl-group donation.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on amino-acid metabolism as the dominant perturbed subsystem in the treatment group. RaMP multi-database ORA ranked KEGG:map00260 "Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism" first with FDR 8.6e-17 and 7 of the input metabolites as hits (glycine, choline, adenosine, L-serine, L-cysteine, L-threonine, and S-adenosylmethionine). The same ORA ranked KEGG:map00270 "Methionine Metabolism" ninth with FDR 1.05e-14 and 6 hits, while the MUMM namespace network from mummichog confirmed glycine-serine-alanine-threonine metabolism as the top network hit (p=0.004, 8-of-8 metabolite overlap) and methionine-and-cysteine-metabolism second (p=0.013, 6-of-6 overlap). Tyrosine metabolism captured the 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde input in the mummichog network (p=0.053, 3-of-3 overlap). The convergence across ORA and m/z-directed network paradigms identifies glycine, L-serine, and S-adenosylmethionine as the primary driver metabolites, connected through enzymes SHMT (R01500), GNMT (R04285), CBS (R01127), and MAT1A (R00587) that convert serine, glycine, and methionine into methyl-donor intermediates. The treatment group therefore shows a coordinated perturbation of one-carbon amino-acid metabolism and methyl-group donation.
